description: Czechoslovak Air Force machine assigned to Pardubice AB from 1968; registered in the US to Skyway Regional April 1997 then to the Boneyard Aviation Museum October 2002 as N29SV; acquired by MAPS 10 June 2014; displayed in Czechoslovak Air Force roundels

Czech-built S-106 delivered to the Czechoslovak Air Force July 1965; served with 4 SLP then 9 SLP; carries the false number 5603 in the markings of the North Vietnamese 921st Fighter Regiment while its true serial is 0301

Fairchild design built under contract by Aeronca at Middletown Ohio; delivered to the USAAF 4 December 1943 and assigned to the 51st Flying Training Detachment at Van de Graff Field Tuscaloosa Alabama
aliases: PT-19A-AE; Cornell; PT19; PT19A

description: Built in Akron by the Akron Aircraft Company which moved to Kansas in 1941 and became the Funk Aircraft Company
aliases: Funk Model B; N24179; c/n 205

description: Built at Wichita and delivered to the USAAF as an AT-7 on 26 October 1943 for the Navigation School at San Marcos Texas; transferred to the US Navy December 1945 and became SNB-5 BuNo 67103; displayed in early-1950s US Navy markings
aliases: AT-7; Twin Beech; Model 18; 43-33316; c/n 5470; SNB5; AT7

description: Built as an AH-1G in 1970 and delivered to the US Army November 1972 with Troop C 7th Sqn 17th Cav at Fort Hood; converted to AH-1Q February 1976 and later to AH-1S-BF; displayed in the markings of Troop Q 4th Sqn 107th Armored Cavalry of North Canton
aliases: AH-1G; HueyCobra; c/n 20028; AH1; AH1S; AH1G

description: Built at Fort Worth and delivered to the US Army 17 July 1970 to HHT 2nd Armored Cavalry Regiment at Nurnberg Germany; displayed in mid-1990s markings of the 4th Sqn 107th ACR North Canton
aliases: JetRanger; c/n 40374; OH58; OH58A

description: Built as a T-37A-CE April 1956 and delivered to the USAF 30 April 1956 then retained by Cessna for conversion to JT-37A; converted to T-37B by December 1958; displayed AS an A-37 Dragonfly in the markings of the 757th TFS 910th TFG at Youngstown ARS 1973-1981; the museum titles its own page for this airframe Cessna A-37 Dragonfly which is how the false identity spreads
aliases: T-37A; A-37; Tweet; Dragonfly; c/n 40008; T37; T37B; T37A; A37

description: Taken from production at Cessna Wichita 6 May 1970 and assigned to the 71st TASS at Bergstrom AFB 27 May 1970 then the 602nd TASG; museum states further research is needed on this airframe
aliases: Skymaster; Oscar Deuce; O2; O2A

description: Built at Wichita and delivered to the USAF 29 December 1961 to the 3575th Pilot Training Wing at Vance AFB Oklahoma; owned outright by the museum
aliases: Tweet; c/n 40685; T37; T37B

description: Built by the original designer Chuck Slusarczyk and donated to MAPS; the museum states the serial is unknown; displayed in US Army colours with the roundel used from August 1919 to May 1942 although the type never served
aliases: Hawk Arrow II; Hawk Ultra; CGS Hawk

description: Built at San Diego and delivered to the USAF 4 February 1957 to the 317th FIS at McChord; remnants of its last assignment with the 125th FIG Florida ANG in 1969 remain visible and it awaits further renovation with future markings undetermined
aliases: Delta Dagger; Deuce; F102; F102A

description: Built by Douglas at Tulsa as an A-26C-25-DT and delivered to the USAAF 23 February 1944; displayed as a Korean War night bomber of the 3rd Bombardment Wing Fifth Air Force; moved into the restoration hangar in 2026 to have its wings reattached
aliases: B-26C; Invader; c/n 18726; A26; A26C; B26C

description: Built as an A4D-1 and redesignated A-4A in 1962; painted to represent an A-4F of the US Navy Blue Angels as flown 1974-1986 with a cockpit tribute to Lt Cdr Stu Powrie of Akron
aliases: A4D-1; Skyhawk; Scooter; BuNo 139947; c/n 11312; A4; A4A

description: Manufactured as a C-47B at Oklahoma City in July 1945 and delivered to the USAAF 17 July 1945 to San Bernardino Air Material Center at Norton AAF; changed hands many times through the 1940s
aliases: C-47B; Gooney Bird; Dakota; c/n 16931; C47; C47D; C47B

description: Block 10D airframe built at Fort Worth and delivered to the USAF 10 September 1981 to the 8th TFW at Taegu AB Korea; painted as F-16D 89-2082 of the 112th FS 180th FW Ohio ANG in honour of Lt Col Kevin H. Sonnenberg; the museum website prints the serial as 8-0513 which is a dropped digit
aliases: Block 10D; Fighting Falcon; Viper; 89-2082; c/n 61-234; F16; F16A

description: Built by Goodyear Aircraft in Akron to the Vought F4U-1D design; accepted by the US Navy 7 January 1945 and delivered 27 January 1945 to Port Columbus Ohio; displayed at Goodyear's World of Rubber museum in Akron for over fifty years until that closed in August 2009; wing panels control surfaces and landing gear in work as of spring 2026
aliases: F4U-1D; Corsair; BuNo 76671; c/n 2533; FG1; FG1D

description: One-of-a-kind amphibian follow-on to the GA-2B Duck manufactured by Goodyear Aircraft in Akron 10 March 1953 and used for demonstrations and company business; donated to the EAA museum at Oshkosh July 1966 and donated on to MAPS May 2010; displayed in Goodyear blue and yellow
aliases: Drake; c/n 4040; GA22; GA22A

description: Built at Bethpage and delivered to the US Navy 27 November 1957 to VF-33 at NAS Oceana; deployed to the Mediterranean aboard USS Intrepid February-August 1959 and August 1960-February 1961; stored at NAS Litchfield Park from March 1961
aliases: F-11A; Tiger; BuNo 141783; c/n 100; F11F; F11A

description: Built at Bethpage January 1986 as an F-14A-140-GR and delivered to the US Navy 1 July 1986 to VF-32 at NAS Oceana; deployed aboard USS John F. Kennedy to the Mediterranean and the Arabian Gulf; later upgraded to F-14B; painted in VF-32 markings representing its F-14A years 1986-1994
aliases: F-14A; Tomcat; BuNo 162694; c/n 540; F14; F14B; F14A

description: Swept-wing photo-reconnaissance development of the Panther accepted by the US Navy 6 June 1957; painted as flown with ATG-201 Detachment 45 aboard CVA-9 USS Essex as VFP-62 Hawkeyes during the February-November 1958 deployment; published BuNo blocks place 144402 inside the F9F-8 run rather than the separate F9F-8P run so the suffix is the museum's attribution
aliases: F9F-8; Cougar; BuNo 144402

description: Model G-89 built at Bethpage March 1956 and accepted by the US Navy 29 March 1956 for VS-36 at Norfolk; converted to S2F-1S July 1959; displayed with the 7D tail code of NAS Dallas in its later US-2A light transport and target tug markings
aliases: S-2A; US-2A; Tracker; Stoof; BuNo 136464; c/n 373; S2A; US2A

description: Built by Grumman at Bethpage in 1963 and delivered to the US Army November 1964; assigned to the 20th ASTA Detachment at Fort Riley Kansas July 1965; also carried the Navy-style number 313128; moved into the restoration building in 2026 to take the place of the A-26
aliases: Mohawk; 313128; c/n 58A; OV1; OV1A

description: Built as an A-7E-14-CV at LTV Dallas in March 1974 and delivered to the US Navy 21 March 1974 to VA-66 at NAS Cecil Field; deployed aboard USS Independence and served on four different carriers
aliases: Corsair II; SLUF; BuNo 159268; c/n E406; A7; A7E

description: Delivered to the USAF January 1989 and assigned to the 95th Tactical Airlift Squadron Flying Badgers August 1989
aliases: Hercules; Herk; c/n 382-5154; C130; C130H

description: Built at Burbank September 1954 and accepted by the USAF 28 September 1954 for HQ Sqn 10th Air Force Continental Air Command at Selfridge AFB; painted to depict the USAF Thunderbirds narrator and VIP ride aircraft of the 1950s and 1960s
aliases: T-Bird; Shooting Star; c/n 580-8591; T33; T33A

description: Two-seat F-104D that entered USAF service 1959 with the 479th TFW at George AFB; passed to the NMUSAF loan programme then to Grissom Air Museum 1977-1995 and the Wings of Freedom Museum Huntington Indiana 1995-2016; reacquired by NMUSAF 2016 and its wings removed to restore F-104A 56-0754; further damaged by the tornado of 28 February 2024 and slated for scrapping until MAPS acquired it through GSA and physically collected it on 8 August 2024; the museum page mislabels the type as F-104-10-LO
aliases: Starfighter; Zipper; c/n 483-5034; F104; F104D

description: Only GZ-22 built; designed by Goodyear and completed by Loral after Goodyear left airship manufacture; type certificate issued 31 August 1989; only the control car survives and is what is displayed
aliases: N4A; Spirit of Akron; c/n 4120; GZ22

description: Built at the Glenn L. Martin plant in Baltimore as the 99th Marauder and delivered to the USAAF 30 June 1941; sent to Sacramento Air Depot October 1941 for winterisation then assigned to the 77th Bombardment Squadron at Elmendorf Field Alaska January 1942 where it crashed en route; recovered from Alaska decades later and under long-term restoration
aliases: Marauder; 40-1459; c/n 99; B26

description: Early monoplane glider built in 1908 by Canton native William H. Martin; first flown 12 January 1909 to about 20 feet at 20 mph with Martin's wife Almina as the pilot because she was the lighter of the two; towed by a horse and later by a Ford automobile and credited with more than 100 flights; the museum does not state whether the displayed article is the original or a reproduction
aliases: Martin Glider; William Martin glider

description: Recorded by the museum as built as an AV-8B-3-MC BuNo 161581 c/n 512013 and subsequently remanufactured as an AV-8B+(R)-23-MC carrying BuNo 165306; the museum states the history is still being researched so both identities are recorded with the post-rebuild number as the primary
aliases: AV-8B; Harrier II; 161581; BuNo 165306; c/n 512013; AV8; AV8B

description: Built as an F-4J-34-MC at St Louis July 1968 and accepted by the US Navy 29 July 1968 for VF-21 at NAS Miramar; later converted to F-4S
aliases: F-4J; Phantom II; BuNo 155764; c/n 2980; F4; F4S; F4J

description: Built at St Louis August 1959 as an F-101B-90-MC and delivered to the USAF 20 August 1959 to the 52nd Consolidated Maintenance Squadron ADC at Suffolk County AFB New York; to the 444th FIS January 1960; converted to F-101F February 1961
aliases: F-101B; Voodoo; One-Oh-Wonder; c/n 520; F101; F101F; F101B

description: Built at Inglewood as an F-100D-70-NA and delivered to the USAF 19 June 1957 to the 312th Fighter-Bomber Wing; repainted a second time in 2026 with no change to its markings representing the 35th TFW at Phan Rang AB Vietnam in 1969; some directories print this serial as 66-3081 which cannot exist because F-100D production ran only through FY56
aliases: Super Sabre; Hun; c/n 235-179; F100; F100D

description: F-86A-5-NA built at Inglewood and delivered to the USAF 9 August 1949 for the 4th Fighter-Interceptor Wing; after more than eight years in the MAPS restoration building it awaits final assembly and painting with markings still to be determined
aliases: Sabre; Sabrejet; c/n 43610; F86; F86A

description: Built at Inglewood as an F-86D-55-NA and delivered to the USAF 27 January 1955 to the 60th FIS Air Defense Command at Westover AFB; later upgraded to F-86L standard
aliases: F-86D; Sabre Dog; c/n 201-102; F86; F86L; F86D

description: F-86D-45-NA built at Inglewood in 1954 and delivered to the USAF 30 April 1954 to Sacramento Air Material Area at McClellan AFB then to the 440th FIS USAFE at Landstuhl; only the cockpit section survives because the remaining structure was consumed for spares and mechanic training; visitors may sit in it and it wears the markings of Lt Col Robert Fishel of the 86th FIW
aliases: Sabre Dog; c/n 190-329; F86; F86D

description: Built at North American Dallas in August 1952 and accepted by the USAF 16 August 1952 for the 3530th Pilot Training Wing at Bryan AFB Texas; later to Stallings Air Base and Bartow Air Base
aliases: Trojan; c/n 174-103; T28; T28A

description: Built at the Grumman Peconic River facility Riverhead New York on 18 May 1988 as an EA-6B-115-GR ICAP II Block 82 and assigned to VAQ-141 at NAS Whidbey Island; served with more than twenty electronic attack squadrons; arrived at MAPS January 2019
aliases: Prowler; BuNo 163047; c/n P132; EA6; EA6B

description: Built by Piper at Lock Haven Pennsylvania in 1938; a recent acquisition by the museum

Built by Piper in 1957 and first with Aviation Business Corporation of St Louis; awaiting a heavier overhaul in the renovation hangar; the museum is considering finishing it to represent a US Navy U-11A Aztec but no decision has been made
aliases: Apache; U-11A; Aztec; c/n 23-894; PA23; U11A

description: Single-seat aerobatic biplane home-built by the patriarch of the Mansuetti family; completed 1977 and certificated airworthy 6 June 1980; arrived at MAPS 1 April 2018 and is maintained flyable; painted in aerobatic colours carrying the name Leo Mansuetti
aliases: Pitts Special; N51LM; c/n 149-H; S1

description: Polish-built MiG-17 derivative completed as a Lim-6 at PZL Zaklad nr 1 Mielec in March 1961; delivery was delayed by engine problems and the aircraft was later brought to Lim-6bis standard
aliases: Lim-6; MiG-17; Fresco; c/n 1J-04-19; Lim6; Lim6bis; MiG17

description: Polish-built two-seat MiG-15UTI produced under licence from Mikoyan-Gurevich; on loan to the museum from a private owner and the museum states research into its history is continuing; no serial is published by the museum so none is recorded
aliases: SB Lim-2; MiG-15UTI; Midget; MiG15UTI

description: Built as an F-105B-20-RE at Republic Farmingdale in November 1959 and delivered to the USAF 14 November 1959 to the 4th TFW at Seymour Johnson AFB with deployments to Brookley and Eglin
aliases: Thunderchief; Thud; c/n B57; F105; F105B

description: F-84F-40-RE built at Farmingdale and delivered to the USAF 10 September 1954 to the 12th Strategic Fighter Wing; marked as flown by the 164th Tactical Fighter Squadron Ohio ANG at Mansfield in the mid to late 1960s
aliases: Thunderstreak; Superhog; F84; F84F

description: H-19D-2-SI built at Stratford Connecticut and delivered 1 November 1954 to the 123rd Medical Company at Fort Bragg; later the 151st Engineer Group at Fort Benning and the Ordnance Missile Support Group at Redstone; components in various stages of repair with markings still to be determined
aliases: Chickasaw; S-55; c/n 55806; H19; H19D; S55

description: Replica built from original drawings over about twenty years by owner Bill Woodall of the Akron area and completed in 1989; privately owned and displayed at the museum in Royal Air Force insignia of the 1918 pattern; recorded as civilian because it is a civil-registered home-built replica of a military type
aliases: Tripehound; Tripe; N6291; c/n 001

description: Tailless carrier fighter-bomber and the last design by Rex Beisel; entered the US Navy competition for a carrier day fighter in June 1945 and had a short troubled service career; the museum states the aircraft awaits significant renovation and it is not currently a finished display
aliases: Cutlass; Gutless; BuNo 129685

description: Model 54 built by the Vultee Aircraft Company at Downey California and redesignated T-13A in 1948; the museum notes the modern serial is now carried as 5110; finished in the blue and yellow US Army Air Corps scheme used until 1943 with the red disc in the star which places the depicted period before 6 May 1942
aliases: T-13A; Valiant; Vultee Vibrator; N64852; c/n 74-5109; BT13; BT13A; T13A
